newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat harvest slow amid intermittent rain.
newsitem.headline: UK wheat harvest slow amid intermittent rain.

text.p: Wheat harvesting in southern Britain has moved slowly in recent days with frequent disruptions from rain, traders and analysts said.
"We've got a stop-start harvest," one trader said. "It's incredibly frustrating. We don't get anything coming onto the market."
"Wheat's very slow," an expert at the agricultural consulting group ADAS, said.
Barley was further on, with most of it cut in the eastern counties of Norfolk and Cambridgeshire, while more rain meant farmers further west had more left to clear.
"The results (on barley) look down quite a bit on last year."

According to ministry figures, the 1996 UK barley crop was 7.78 million tonnes. And according to Home Grown Cereals Authority estimates the area planted for the 1997 crop for the UK as a whole was up by 5.7 percent at 1.338 million hectares.
Much of the wheat was still showing green straw, the ADAS expert said. On early cut wheat yields were down, "but I don't think they are down by perhaps as much as expected," the ADAS expert said.
Wet weather in June had probably saved early crops, but it could also have cut yields on better soils.

He stressed it was too early for meaningful estimates on overall yields, but he was looking for something less than last year's bumper crop. Yields would be 7.8 tonnes per hectare or lower, rather than the 8.12 tonnes achieved in 1996.
Ministry figures show the 1996 UK wheat crop at 16.1 million tonnes. According to the Home Grown Cereals Authority, this year's UK wheat area is up by 2.5 percent at 2.026 million hectares.
